title: Tenali and the Pot of Gold at Rainbow End

keywords: tenali and the pot of gold at rainbow end
full_text:
A gullible, greedy courtier named Somadatta was obsessed with old folklore tales of pots of gold buried where rainbows touch the earth. Whenever a monsoon shower passed over Vijayanagara and a colorful rainbow arched across the sky, Somadatta would abandon his court duties, mount his horse, and gallop frantically across hills, streams, and muddy ditches, trying to reach the foot of the rainbow!
Every time, the rainbow receded into the distance, leaving Somadatta bruised, soaking wet, and covered in mud.

Yet Somadatta insisted: 'Yesterday I saw the rainbow touching the eastern hills! Next time, I will ride faster and seize the gold!'

King Krishnadevaraya, amused by the courtier’s folly, asked Tenali Raman to cure him.

Tenali went to Somadatta’s house with an ancient-looking parchment map:
'Friend Somadatta, thou hast been searching in the wrong place!
Rainbows are celestial bridges; they touch the earth only when the soil has been thoroughly tilled, turned, and aerated!
Look at this neglected five-acre field behind thy estate.
The ancient astrological map states that if thou diggest three feet deep across this entire field with a spade before the next rain, the next rainbow will deposit its pot of gold directly in the center!'

Somadatta’s eyes widened with greed: 'Is this true, Tenali?'
'Upon my honor!' affirmed Tenali. 'Grab a spade and dig!'

For two months, Somadatta, who had never done a day’s manual work in his life, went out at dawn with a spade.
He dug, turned the heavy soil, removed stones, broke clods, and channeled water ditches, sweating profusely, his soft hands blistering and then hardening into strong, capable palms.
He dug up every single foot of the five-acre field three feet deep!

When the field was completely tilled, Tenali visited him carrying two sacks of prime wheat seed:
'Now, Somadatta, to attract the rainbow’s golden light, scatter these golden seeds across the plowed soil!'
Somadatta eagerly sowed the wheat.

The monsoon rains arrived. The seeds sprouted, and within four months, the entire field became an ocean of rich, golden, heavy-eared wheat!
When the harvest was reaped and sold at the market, Somadatta received two hundred gold dinars in cash!

Somadatta stood holding his heavy purse of real gold coins, looking at his fertile land.
Tenali walked up to him with a warm smile:
'Where is the rainbow, Somadatta?'

Somadatta laughed heartily, wiping sweat from his brow:
'Tenali, the rainbow was in the sweat of my own brow!
I chased colored light across the clouds and found only mud. But when I put my spade into the earth, the true pot of gold sprouted from the soil!'

Somadatta was cured of his foolish superstition, becoming an industrious farmer and a respected counselor in the imperial court.
moral: Chasing illusory promises of effortless wealth leads to exhaustion; honest labor is the only true pot of gold.
